Because our well-being wasn’t directly at stake, we reinforced the habit of staying silent. As a Black woman, even though I understand systemic marginalization, my family's financial stability still allowed me to observe these specific local immigration tensions from a distance without feeling erased. The pressure to belong without engaging remains a skill I carry from childhood.

reflexivity_response: My background heavily shaped how I read these posts, particularly my tendency to separate blunt political policy language from active harm. Growing up in a community that avoided open conflict taught me to observe debates quietly and look at them analytically from a distance. This balance allowed me to distinguish between standard political frustration and genuine, targeted hostility.
